facts.fact: The StackAdapt blog article 'How to use zero-party data to personalize your campaigns' was published on 2021-08-05.

Zero-party data is defined as information a customer proactively volunteers to share with a brand, through formats such as quizzes, contests, personalized surveys, opt-in forms, or other personalized communications.
facts.quote: Zero-party data is the information that a customer proactively volunteers to share with a brand

facts.fact: First-party data is defined as information a company collects and owns about customers' behaviours and actions on its website (pixel data), app, social media, or other mediums where they engage or transact with the brand.
facts.quote: about your customers’ behaviours and actions on your website (pixel data), app, social media, or other mediums

facts.fact: Second-party data is defined as information similar to first-party data that a company owns but that is collected by another organization it partners or transacts with.
facts.quote: Information (similar to 1st-party data) that you own, however, is collected by another organization that you partner or transact with.

facts.fact: Third-party data is defined as information collected and sold by independent organizations and available to layer onto advertising initiatives.
facts.quote: Information collected and sold by independent organizations available to you to layer onto your advertising initiatives.

facts.fact: Discovery ads are defined by StackAdapt as interactive ads that encourage users to engage with the ad and provide information, generally regarding a preference or opinion.
facts.quote: Discovery ads are interactive ads that encourage users to engage with the ad and provide information
